items.title: Evaluate media probing and normalization tools
acceptance_criteria: At least three viable approaches are compared using current official documentation.
Comparison covers supported containers/codecs, metadata accuracy, malformed-input exposure, sandboxability, deployment footprint, performance, and license implications.
Recommendation distinguishes metadata inspection from transcoding/normalization.
A reproducible proof-of-concept plan and known limitations are documented.

items.title: Implement isolated media inspection and validation adapter
acceptance_criteria: The adapter derives authoritative media metadata from file bytes rather than client hints.
Metadata validation covers container, duration, byte size, sample rate, channels, and audio-track presence.
A separate full-file decode gate detects malformed and truncated audio; metadata probing alone is never treated as full decode validation.
Failures use stable error codes and bounded probe/decode time, input size, probe parameters, and output.
Fixtures and tests cover valid media, malformed metadata, unsupported containers, truncated media, and limit-exceeding inputs.

items.title: Define object storage port and implement local filesystem adapter
acceptance_criteria: A provider-neutral object storage port defines put, get/open, head, and delete operations without exposing provider SDK types.
The local adapter writes atomically, prevents path traversal, verifies content length/checksum, and supports idempotent object keys.
Tests cover overwrite/conflict policy, missing objects, corrupted checksums, path traversal, interrupted writes, and deletion.
Storage references remain opaque and compatible with AudioAsset v1.

src/voxpipe/storage/local.py — atomic local filesystem adapter with SHA-256, size limits, idempotency, conflict and path/symlink protection

docs/architecture/storage.md — boundary and deployment limitations

items.title: Implement batch ingestion application service
acceptance_criteria: The service accepts a staged local media file and authenticated tenant context, not a client-controlled filesystem path.
It creates an idempotent session, probes metadata, performs full decode validation, computes SHA-256, and stores the immutable asset.
Session and asset lifecycle transitions are explicit and invalid transitions fail closed.
Failures trigger bounded cleanup/compensation and never leave a completed session without an accepted asset.
Unit and integration tests cover duplicate requests, storage failures, parser failures, and tenant mismatch.
evidence: src/voxpipe/ingestion/service.py — batch orchestration, staging-root enforcement, SHA-256 request fingerprint, state transitions, idempotency, tenant scoping, asset creation, and compensation

contracts/schemas/ingestion-session.v1.schema.json — retention policy and allowlisted declared_by source metadata
tests/test_ingestion_service.py — schema validation, idempotent replay/conflict, tenant isolation, path protection, probe/decode/storage failures, staged mutation, cleanup, and repository reopen

items.title: Add stale ingestion recovery, leases, and orphan reconciliation
acceptance_criteria: Workers claim active sessions with unique expiring lease owners; concurrent claims fail closed and state updates use compare-and-swap.
Sessions persist only a relative private staging reference; expired leases can resume the same asset ID/object key without duplicate assets.
Recovery handles restart points before storage, after object write, and after asset metadata commit.
A failed-session reconciler retries cleanup of associated object bytes and asset metadata and returns a structured audit report.
Fault-injection tests cover live lease contention, expired lease recovery, missing staged files, session expiry, and orphan cleanup.
evidence: src/voxpipe/ingestion/repository.py — atomic expiring lease claims, per-attempt ownership, recoverable-session scans, and state-scoped reconciliation queries

src/voxpipe/ingestion/service.py — relative private staging references, lease refresh at transitions, resumable processing with stable asset IDs/timestamps, expiry handling, and idempotent storage/metadata replay

contracts/schemas/ingestion-session.v1.schema.json — validated staging_reference and lease contracts
tests/test_ingestion_recovery.py — exclusive claim, lease expiry, live lease, recovery at finalizing/processing/object/asset boundaries, missing staging, expiry, and orphan cleanup

items.title: Expose authenticated batch upload API and durable ingestion job queue
acceptance_criteria: Upload initiation, streamed byte transfer, finalization, status, and cancellation have versioned API contracts.
Tenant identity is derived only from authenticated context; arbitrary client filesystem paths and storage keys are never accepted.
A PostgreSQL-backed queue uses atomic claims, expiring leases, bounded retries, and a dead-letter state.
API requests return durable session/job identifiers and do not hold HTTP connections open for media processing.
Integration tests cover duplicate upload requests, interrupted transfers, worker restart, cancellation races, tenant isolation, and retry exhaustion.

tests/test_ingestion_worker.py — worker success, retry classification, dead-letter, stale lease, and tenant/worker identity tests

internal/httpapi/server_test.go — duplicate upload, interrupted transfer, client-controlled retention rejection, upload/cancellation race with no orphaned staged bytes, authorization, and API lifecycle tests

items.title: Standardize autonomous agent workflows, skills, and independent CI gates
acceptance_criteria: Repository skills under .agents/skills define reusable task execution, CI triage, PostgreSQL reliability, and cross-runtime contract workflows with valid discovery metadata.
Project-scoped read-only specialist agents exist for CI triage, security review, and cross-runtime contract review.
AGENTS.md and the execution protocol explain skill selection, safe delegation, reviewer independence, and fallback behavior when subagents are unavailable.
Repository validation checks skill and custom-agent metadata so malformed or missing agent assets fail locally and in CI.
Python and Go CI gates run independently; superseded feature-branch runs are cancelled rather than duplicated.
Go validation is read-only and checks module drift, formatting, vet, and race-enabled tests.

items.title: Reconcile staged uploads and enforce retention and deletion
acceptance_criteria: A bounded, tenant-scoped reconciler identifies abandoned temporary uploads and staged sources using database state and explicit retention policy.
The reconciler never deletes bytes for a session with an active upload or valid worker lease; row locking and state checks make cleanup race-safe.
Terminal cancellation, expiry, permanent failure, and successful object publication have explicit staging cleanup rules.
Retention and deletion propagate across staging, object storage, metadata, and derived artifacts with idempotent retries.
Every cleanup/deletion outcome emits an auditable event without logging transcript or audio contents.
PostgreSQL integration tests cover process crashes, concurrent upload/finalize/cancel, expired sessions, partial files, repeated cleanup, and deletion failures.
evidence: Migration 0004 adds forced-RLS upload leases and tenant-scoped audit events.
API upload leases fence concurrent transfers and finalization; lease duration exceeds session expiry and expired leases fence cleanup.
Reconciliation expires stale unfinalized sessions, removes completed/terminal staging and interrupted parts, and deletes retained objects before metadata.
VOXPIPE_DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS assigns server-authoritative asset expiry; 0 disables automatic asset expiry.
Python unit/PostgreSQL integration and Go race/PostgreSQL integration passed on CI run 44469883406 (head 2604e32ebd438e98cb505529cc9e3082fb02bc53).
PR #24 follow-up hardening: compensation cleanup now deletes object bytes before metadata and retains metadata if object deletion fails; regression tests enforce the ordering.

items.title: Harden production identity and upload abuse controls
acceptance_criteria: Production authentication validates trusted issuer, audience, expiry, not-before, signing-key rotation, tenant mapping, and scopes; invalid or unavailable identity metadata fails closed.
Per-tenant quotas bound concurrent uploads, total staged bytes, and ingestion rate.
Upload body reads have explicit duration/inactivity bounds without breaking legitimate large streaming transfers.
Rate limits and resource limits are enforced before expensive media processing and return stable retryable error codes.
Retention policy, storage keys, and filesystem paths remain server-authoritative.
Security tests cover expired/revoked tokens, wrong audience/issuer, key rotation, cross-tenant tokens, slow uploads, quota exhaustion, and concurrent abuse.
evidence: internal/httpapi/oidc.go and oidc_test.go — RS256 JWKS validation, exact issuer/audience and time claims, UUID tenant mapping, allowlisted scopes, active-token introspection/revocation checks, key rotation refresh, and fail-closed provider errors.

internal/httpapi/store.go — PostgreSQL advisory-lock reservations for staged bytes and rolling ingestion rate, plus concurrent upload lease quotas; terminal staging reservations remain counted until cleanup reconciliation records completion.
internal/httpapi/upload_limits.go and server.go — resettable inactivity and absolute upload deadlines, stable 408/429 errors, and server-authoritative limits.

internal/httpapi/store_integration_test.go, upload_limits_test.go, and server_test.go — staged-byte, rate, concurrent-upload, slow-body, OIDC claims/revocation/rotation, and server-authoritative policy coverage.
GitHub Actions run 44525504449 — both independent Python/PostgreSQL 16 and Go/PostgreSQL 16 jobs passed on exact PR head 68e35212d8f94a0c64f7cbb0b3a2659bbd4aa08b.

PR #21 Go OIDC implementation verified: RS256-only JWT, HTTPS issuer/JWKS/introspection endpoints, exact issuer/audience, exp/nbf, minimum 2048-bit RSA keys, per-request introspection, signing-key refresh, allowlisted scopes, and fail-closed behavior.

items.title: Harden worker supervision and queue observability
acceptance_criteria: Transient database/network failures during claim, heartbeat, failure recording, and completion do not silently terminate the worker process; retries use bounded backoff and jitter.
Heartbeat failure tracking stops processing or fences acknowledgement when the worker can no longer prove lease ownership.
Queue depth, oldest pending age, active leases, retry counts, dead-letter counts, and processing duration are observable per tenant without exposing audio or transcript content.
Worker shutdown is graceful and leaves jobs recoverable after process termination.
Failure-injection tests cover database outages, heartbeat loss, lease expiry during processing, worker restart, and graceful shutdown.
evidence: src/voxpipe/ingestion/worker.py — heartbeat safety-window fencing, bounded exponential retry with jitter, tenant-scoped counters, and supervised polling across transient claim/failure/completion outages.
src/voxpipe/ingestion/jobs.py and migration 0005 — durable tenant-scoped queue health metrics and per-attempt started_at timestamps for processing-duration measurement.

scripts/run_ingestion_worker.py — signal-driven graceful stop; scripts/inspect_ingestion_queue.py — tenant-scoped operator CLI for queue depth, age, active leases, retries, dead letters, and processing duration.
tests/test_ingestion_worker.py and tests/test_postgres_repository.py — heartbeat loss, claim/failure/completion outages, shutdown, lease reclaim, tenant metrics, retries, and dead-letter coverage.
GitHub Actions run 44525504449 — both independent Python/PostgreSQL 16 and Go/PostgreSQL 16 jobs passed on exact PR head 68e35212d8f94a0c64f7cbb0b3a2659bbd4aa08b.

PR #21 worker reliability verified: lease heartbeat safety-window fencing, bounded jittered supervisor backoff, graceful signal stop, durable tenant-scoped PostgreSQL metrics; no public unauthenticated metrics endpoint.

items.title: Define canonical transcript contract and provider-neutral speech-to-text port
acceptance_criteria: A versioned transcript schema defines asset linkage, language, ordered segments, optional word timestamps, speaker references, confidence, and provider/model/audio-hash provenance.
A provider-neutral SpeechToTextPort accepts an extracted readable audio stream and explicit language/word-timing/diarization options without filesystem paths, tenant IDs, or vendor SDK types.
A shared validator enforces timestamp ordering/duration bounds, speaker references, unique IDs, confidence ranges, timezone-aware provenance, and requested asset binding.
Stable transcription error codes expose retryability and optional retry-after without raw provider payloads or secrets.
Schema fixtures and offline adapter contract tests run without external providers, model downloads, or paid inference.
evidence: contracts/schemas/transcript.v1.schema.json and contracts/examples/transcript.valid.json — canonical transcript wire contract and valid fixture.
src/voxpipe/speech/contracts.py, ports.py, and service.py — immutable provider-neutral request/result types, stable errors, adapter protocol, and output validation.
tests/test_speech_contracts.py and tests/test_contract_schemas.py — offline validation and adapter boundary tests.

GitHub Actions run 44527653554 — both Python/PostgreSQL 16 and Go/PostgreSQL 16 jobs passed on exact head 348cac515723105e246db6f42550c5934add226d; transcript schema, provider-neutral port, cross-field validator, and offline adapter contract tests were included.

items.title: Evaluate speech-to-text providers and implement the first adapter
acceptance_criteria: At least three viable local or hosted STT approaches are compared using current official documentation and a reproducible evaluation plan.
Evaluation covers Persian and multilingual quality evidence, word timestamps, diarization, supported formats, latency, privacy/data handling, deployment, licensing, and total cost.
Provider selection is recorded in an ADR and does not assume paid inference or external data transfer without explicit authorization.
The selected adapter implements SpeechToTextPort without leaking vendor SDK types into application contracts.
Provider errors map to stable VoxPipe transcription error codes with retryability and bounded retry-after semantics.
Offline contract tests cover request options, result validation, provenance binding, and provider failure mapping; any live integration test is opt-in and does not require secrets in CI.

A repeatable scoring harness reports normalized Persian-aware WER/CER, real-time factor, and optional estimated API cost from versioned per-file JSONL results; unmeasured model quality is not fabricated.
evidence: docs/research/stt-provider-evaluation.md and ADR-0022 — three viable local/hosted STT approaches compared using official documentation; local Faster-Whisper selected without hosted inference or customer-audio egress.
scripts/run_fleurs_stt_benchmark.py and scripts/benchmark_stt.py — pinned FLEURS fa_ir test harness, Persian normalization, per-file WER/CER/RTF, word timestamps and corpus manifest generation.

GitHub Actions run 44849751146 passed end-to-end: 100 FLEURS Persian test items, dataset revision 6989e5bd2dc37546a93ae5d857bc04325e6a3738, model revision 536b0662742c02347bc0e980a01041f333bce120, model.bin SHA-256 recorded.

Quality warning: the measured WER is too high for production; model-quality improvement is a follow-up, not an unmeasured claim.

Verified benchmark run 44911440709 on commit 614d7133d87e00a2c3e619258806ab957b85980a is re-running the 100-sample benchmark with immutable action pins and artifact provenance. Previous completed run 44849751146 on commit 43a57046abc31892034cbd587bfd0b8e82d33cfc measured normalized WER 52.24%, CER 16.43%, RTF 0.1652, and p50/p95 latency 2.52/3.78 seconds. This is reproducible evidence, but WER remains too high for production.

items.title: Evaluate and implement VAD
acceptance_criteria: Compare at least two VAD approaches on licensed speech data.
Report speech-region precision/recall, boundary error, false activation, missed speech, runtime and memory.
Expose a provider-neutral VAD contract and deterministic offline tests.
Document failure behavior for silence, music, overlap and noisy input.
evidence: src/voxpipe/speech/vad.py — provider-neutral Silero and WebRTC adapters plus frame-level metric evaluator and overlap-aware region matching.
tests/test_speech_intelligence.py — offline tests cover region conversion, frame metrics and best-overlap boundary matching.

scripts/run_fleurs_vad_benchmark.py and benchmarks/results/fleurs-vad-2026-11-21/summary.json — 60 pinned FLEURS utterances compared on CPU; WebRTC envelope-proxy F1 0.888 and Silero 0.837, with boundary/runtime/false-activation/missed-speech/RSS measurements.
GitHub Actions run 44848923641 — successful two-model FLEURS VAD envelope-proxy benchmark.

Action-pinned rerun 44911001571 succeeded on commit 36aa4e977de32f0417dcbb11bf4325762a6bedc6. On 60 FLEURS utterances, WebRTC reported precision 0.991, recall 0.813, F1 0.888, envelope-boundary error 481 ms, false activation 5.77 s and missed speech 153.3 s; Silero F1 was 0.837. These are utterance-envelope proxy metrics, not frame-level ground truth.
items.blocked_reason: FLEURS has utterance-level references, not frame-level speech/non-speech annotations. Current precision/recall are explicitly envelope-proxy scores; true Persian frame-labelled VAD acceptance is still required. Silence/music/overlap/noisy failure modes need dedicated labelled tests.

items.title: Evaluate speaker diarization
acceptance_criteria: Compare at least two diarization approaches with speaker-labelled consented audio.
Report DER and JER with documented collar/overlap policy and speaker-count error.
Preserve speaker identity only within an asset; do not infer real-world identity.
Expose a provider-neutral diarization result and failure contract.
evidence: src/voxpipe/speech/diarization.py — provider-neutral diarization result, local ECAPA embeddings, deterministic cosine clustering and DER/JER evaluation.
scripts/run_neyshekar_diarization_benchmark.py — threshold selected on Neyshekar validation speakers and evaluated on disjoint test speakers.

benchmarks/results/neyshekar-v6-diarization-2026-11-21/summary.json — validation-selected threshold 0.20; held-out synthetic test DER 23.81%, JER 23.60%; single-speaker baseline DER 57.14%, JER 85.71%; speaker-count error 2.
GitHub Actions run 44848021967 — successful controlled Persian diarization benchmark using anonymous CC0 Neyshekar V6.0 speaker labels.

Action-pinned rerun 44911007178 succeeded on commit 3dfddd7235f411a4a70fb2053519bdea4e649795. It reproduces the controlled Neyshekar V6.0 synthetic-speaker evaluation; the held-out split contains six short read-speech clips and does not represent natural overlapping conversation.
items.blocked_reason: Current evaluation is a synthetic concatenation of read-speech clips, not naturally recorded multi-speaker conversation; the source does not provide explicit per-speaker consent records or overlap annotations. Natural conversation, overlap and explicit consent remain acceptance gates.

items.title: Implement language identification
acceptance_criteria: Evaluate language identification on Persian, English and code-switched audio.
Report macro-F1, confusion matrix, confidence calibration and segment-level boundary behavior.
Support unknown/uncertain outcomes; never force a language label below a configured threshold.
Expose a provider-neutral language-identification contract and tests.
evidence: src/voxpipe/speech/language_id.py — local SpeechBrain VoxLingua107 adapter, threshold-based und outcome, sliding-window support and confidence-calibration evaluator.

scripts/run_fleurs_lid_benchmark.py and benchmarks/results/fleurs-lid-2026-11-21/summary.json — pinned FLEURS fa_ir/en_us/de_de benchmark (20 samples per language); accuracy 95%, strict union-label macro-F1 0.7297, ECE 0.0445; Persian and English 20/20, German 17/20.
GitHub Actions run 44847915953 — successful CPU-only local SpeechBrain benchmark; no hosted inference.

Action-pinned rerun 44910995917 succeeded on commit 7450a4a6d81c2dcd6699b94eeb20428f292d366b. On 60 FLEURS samples (20 each Persian, English and German), accuracy was 95%, strict union-label macro-F1 0.7297 and ECE 0.0445. Threshold 0.0 means abstention was not calibrated; three German clips were incorrectly classified as Romanian.

items.title: Create consented speech evaluation corpus governance
acceptance_criteria: Record source, license, consent basis, dataset revision, split, speaker/session identity and checksum for each item.
Separate public benchmark data from customer data and prevent customer audio entering public evaluation by default.
Validate dataset manifest and reject unlicensed or untraceable audio/reference pairs.
Document deletion, attribution and redistribution restrictions.
evidence: contracts/schemas/speech-corpus-manifest.v1.schema.json and scripts/validate_corpus_manifest.py — versioned manifest validation for dataset revision, license, attribution, consent basis, source-file SHA-256 and per-item audio/reference hashes.

docs/research/corpus-governance.md — separates public benchmark and customer audio; documents attribution, deletion, retention, redistribution and limits of public-license versus individual-consent evidence.
FLEURS ASR benchmark generated a manifest for 100 fa_ir test items with pinned revision and per-item hashes; the successful CI artifact is attached to run 44848225647.
FLEURS and Neyshekar benchmark sources are pinned to CC BY 4.0 and CC0-1.0 respectively; no customer audio is used.

benchmarks/corpora/proxies/fleurs-fa-ir-20.json — 20-item Public Dataset Proxy derived from the pinned FLEURS fa_ir test artifact (run 44848225647, artifact 14683554273); includes stable IDs, source revision, CC BY 4.0 attribution, per-audio and reference SHA-256, exact reference text, and accept/reject policy; reference hashes verified against UTF-8 text. Not human-reviewed gold and not individual consent evidence.
items.blocked_reason: The 20-item Public Dataset Proxy is a minimal reproducibility/governance fallback only. Public licensing does not establish individual speaker consent; natural conversational data with explicit consent and deletion/redistribution evidence remains required for full corpus-governance acceptance.

src/voxpipe/structuring/service.py and contracts.py — provider-neutral typed extraction, exact source evidence validation, allowed-field enforcement and prompt-injection-resistant data boundary.

items.title: Implement tenant-isolated transcript persistence
acceptance_criteria: Persist transcript revisions, segments, words, speakers and provenance in PostgreSQL.
Apply forced RLS and tenant-scoped foreign keys to all transcript-derived records.
Enforce idempotent writes, immutable source linkage and retention/deletion propagation.

evidence: migrations/postgres/0006_create_tenant_transcripts.sql — tenant-scoped immutable transcript revisions, speakers, segments and words; forced RLS; append-only app grants; source-asset deletion cascade.

src/voxpipe/ingestion/postgres.py — create_transcript_revision atomically validates and inserts a complete revision; identical retries return the stored revision while conflicting content is rejected; get_transcript_revision reads an explicit or latest revision under transaction-local tenant context.
src/voxpipe/ingestion/repository.py and src/voxpipe/ingestion/__init__.py — provider-neutral TranscriptRepositoryPort exported separately from the SQLite ingestion repository.

tests/test_postgres_repository.py — PostgreSQL integration coverage for identical retries, conflicting writes, concurrent same-revision writers, explicit/latest revision reads, words/speakers, no-context RLS write denial, cross-tenant source-asset FK rejection, cross-tenant reads and deletion propagation.

items.title: Implement hybrid and semantic retrieval
acceptance_criteria: Compare PostgreSQL full-text and pgvector hybrid retrieval against a versioned relevance set.
Support lexical/vector fusion, tenant/source/time/speaker/entity filters and explainable provenance.
Report Recall@k, MRR/nDCG, latency and index/storage cost.
Test RLS, embedding version migration, stale-index cleanup and deletion propagation.
evidence: 2026-11-22: added provider-neutral Embedding/semantic-search ports, authenticated tenant/source/time/speaker/entity filter contract, immutable source-attributed candidate contract, deterministic weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, duplicate/provenance conflict rejection, and unit tests. This is the retrieval orchestration/fusion foundation only; no pgvector storage adapter or measured relevance benchmark is claimed.

2026-11-22: added PostgreSQL pgvector 0.8.7-backed 384-dimensional segment embedding storage with HNSW cosine index, model/version isolation, source-text SHA binding, forced tenant RLS, transcript/asset deletion cascade, filtered semantic search, and tenant-scoped obsolete-version cleanup. Added Recall@K/MRR/nDCG evaluator and pgvector integration tests. Embedding generation/model selection and a labelled relevance corpus remain separate gates.

CI triage: first pgvector integration run confirmed semantic ranking, tenant filtering, source binding and stale-version deletion path. Two test/permission issues were corrected: the evaluator's Recall@2 expected value was 0.75 (not 1.0) for the defined ranked lists, and the RLS-scoped application role needed DELETE permission on the embeddings table for tenant-scoped model-version cleanup. No tenant or source isolation was relaxed.

2026-11-23: Added LocalSentenceTransformerEmbeddingAdapter for query/document embeddings from a pre-provisioned local model directory, explicit query/document prefixes, model/version attribution, configured-dimension checks, finite/unit-norm validation, and no runtime weight downloads. Exported from voxpipe.retrieval; added tests/test_local_retrieval_embeddings.py for prefixing, provenance, malformed outputs, and local-only model provisioning. No production embedding model is selected and no relevance quality is claimed.

2026-11-23: Exact PR head with LocalSentenceTransformerEmbeddingAdapter, package export, tests/test_local_retrieval_embeddings.py and architecture/ledger updates passed Validate run 45138651058 (Python/PostgreSQL and Go/PostgreSQL).

2026-11-23: Added a PostgreSQL/pgvector integration test that creates local query/document vectors through LocalSentenceTransformerEmbeddingAdapter, stores the document vector and retrieves it with the query vector under tenant/language filters. The fake encoder avoids model downloads while verifying the real adapter-to-database contract; no retrieval relevance claim is made.
items.blocked_reason: A local-only SentenceTransformer adapter now exists, but a production multilingual model is not selected or provisioned. Persian model quality/latency/storage benchmarking, a versioned human-judged relevance set, entity-index filters, and index rebuild/recall benchmarking remain.
